それに.en: それに means ‘moreover’ and is used to add more information to a statement. We're looking for a grammar point that presents a situation and then explains how that situation was or will be resolved.

ところで.en: ところで means 'by the way'. and it is only used when introducing new topics, not continuing within the same topic. We are looking for a grammar point that highlights the situation then goes on to explain how that situation was or will be resolved.

そうすると.en: Actions intentionally taken by the speaker cannot follow そうすると. We're looking for a grammar point that presents a situation and then explains how it was or will be resolved.

attributes.translation: I plan to be the top scorer on the test. Therefore, I decided to slightly increase the amount of time I study.
attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase indicating that (A) is the place from which, accordingly, (B). Literally, with that place, (B) is the solution.

attributes.body_ja:
「そこで」は、「そこ」と格助詞（かくじょし）の「で」からできた表現（ひょうげん）で、「それを受（う）けて」「その状態（じょうたい）で」「その状況（じょうきょう）で」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。もともと「そこ」は「その場所（ばしょ）」という意味（いみ）ですが、この場合（ばあい）は「状態（じょうたい）」や「状況（じょうきょう）」を表（あらわ）しています。この文法（ぶんぽう）は、「其処（そこ）で」と書（か）かれることもありますが、非常（ひじょう）に稀（まれ）です。

「そこで」を使（つか）う文（ぶん）では、たいてい、最初（さいしょ）の文（ぶん）である「状況（じょうきょう）」が説明（せつめい）されます。そのあとに「そこで」が続（つづ）いて、その状況（じょうきょう）に対（たい）してどのような行動（こうどう）を起（お）こしたか、または起（お）こすかが述（の）べられます。

この表現（ひょうげん）は、(B) の内容（ないよう）が話（はな）し手（て）の意思（いし）で変（か）えられる行動（こうどう）の場合（ばあい）にだけ使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
そこで (very rarely seen as 其処（そこ）で) is a combination of そこ 'there', and the case marking particle で. It is often translated as 'to that end', or 'accordingly'. Literally, it just means 'at that place', with で's use as 'with' or 'by' highlighting that something will be done there ('there' often being a situation). This phrase behaves very similarly to 'as such' in English.

Usually, a first sentence will highlight what the 'situation' is, before そこで goes on to explain how that situation was or will be resolved.

As で implies the 'use' of something, this expression should only highlight actions that are controllable.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Difference between それで and そこで

attributes.body: These expressions are similar in that both are used at the beginning of a sentence and can express the outcome of a situation, but they differ in nuance. そこで is relatively vague about the connection between the two events, like the English 'as such' or 'accordingly', while その結果 more specifically conveys that a situation or condition results from the previously mentioned cause.

first_relatable.title: そこで
first_relatable.meaning: Accordingly, Now, Therefore, To that end

attributes.body: Both are typically used at the beginning of a sentence to show what follows from a certain cause or situation. そのため(に) more clearly states the relation and can mean either 'due to that' or 'for that purpose', while そこで is less clear about the relationship between the previous thought and what follows, similar to the English 'as such' or 'in light of that'.

first_relatable.title: そこで
first_relatable.meaning: Accordingly, Now, Therefore, To that end

second_relatable.title: そのため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, Because of that, To that end

attributes.body: Both describe what follows from a previous situation, but with different nuance. そこで introduces an intentional response to a situation, e.g. 雨が降ってきた。そこで傘をさした ('It started raining, so I opened my umbrella.') すると shows a natural or immediate result, e.g. 雨が降ってきた。すると子供が泣き出した ('It started raining. Then the child started crying.')

first_relatable.title: そこで
first_relatable.meaning: Accordingly, Now, Therefore, To that end

second_relatable.title: すると
second_relatable.meaning: Having done..., If...is done..., (And/just) then, Thereupon, If so

attributes.body: そこで and したがって are both used at the beginning of a sentence to express one action following another, but differ in nuance and tone. そこで is a general-purpose expression usable in various situations and contexts, like the English 'so' or 'as such'. In contrast, したがって is more formal and has a stricter 'following from that' or 'thus' nuance.
